patterns.title: From insight to execution: AI that acts, not advises
orgs: Kenco (3PL operator, agent count as operating plan)
HubSpot (published agent usage: 19% of Pro+, actions 3.5x)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: seventh consecutive confirming edition; evidence moved from announcements to USAGE — HubSpot published the demand response to per-result pricing (19% of Pro+ using agents, actions 3.5x, credits >2x; S02). Salesforce's supply-chain agent (E07 S01) revealed as a process engine (30+ templates) with a screen-learning integration agent (S04); Globality shipped autonomous sourcing with negotiation inside (S05); Plataine took planning agents to the capital-decision horizon (S10). Counter-current = CONTROL: Amazon admits agents on its own terms (S01); five vendors sell kill switches / rollbacks / runtime guards (S06). Audited customer savings number STILL missing after eight editions. SAP Outbound agent silent a SEVENTH cycle.
confirmers: an audited customer autonomy or savings number (Siemens Erlangen operating results remain the strongest candidate; only the April humanoid trial numbers exist)
a vendor disclosing the PAID share of an agent base separately from trials (HubSpot's 19% is usage share, not paid share)
weakeners: MEASURED INSTANCE LOGGED E07 (S09): verification caps deployment; a second independent study would turn the ceiling into a wall
Q3/Q4 earnings calls re-describing 'agents' as 'assistants' — nothing ran that way in E08

patterns.title: The moat is business context, not the model
orgs: HubSpot (context-completeness score; outcomes tied to context quality)
Emerald Intel (priced market-context product via connector)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: three new voices of different kinds — HubSpot scored context as a product feature ('context completeness') and reported outcomes tracking context quality (vendor analysis, S02); Emerald Intel sells verified cannabis market context to assistants by subscription via MCP (S13) — the external-market half of the confirmer; Noetive raised $41M for an 'intelligence of record' (S11). AVEVA + Cognite: pre-close a THIRD quiet edition; quiet-cycle deep-dive ran (targeted search) and found no packaging news. Direction held at accelerating; promotion bar (>=3 corroborated cycles, >=3 evidence classes, ~2x orgs) now arguably met (5 -> 13 orgs; vendor, operator, venture, analyst, priced-data-product classes) — decide promotion at E09 with one more cycle of evidence.
confirmers: a context layer sold as its own priced SKU for a company's INTERNAL business — Emerald Intel (S13) is the external-market half; AVEVA + Cognite packaging post-close remains the internal candidate (re-scope to any industrial DataOps vendor if quiet again at E09)
weakeners: frontier models reasoning well enough over raw tables that definition layers stop mattering — no evidence; HubSpot's context-quality finding (S02) argues the other way

patterns.title: AI economics shift from seats to outcomes and tokens
orgs: HubSpot (per-result rates + seats-and-credits hybrid, usage disclosed)
GitLab (per-user, per-group agent metering from Oct 19)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: first DEMAND CURVE — HubSpot (S02): per-result pricing since Apr 14 ($0.50/resolved conversation, $1/lead) -> August agent actions 3.5x, credit consumption >2x despite the price cut; hybrid seats-for-people + credits-for-agents is now the STANDARD shape (the weakener's 'floor' is the norm, not a reversion). GitLab meters agent traffic per user/group from Oct 19 (S12). Acumatica AI Unit price STILL unpublished with the R2 launch fixed for Oct 1 (S07) — the mid-market confirmer decides next edition.
confirmers: a published price per AI Unit at the Acumatica 2026 R2 launch on Oct 1 — waited on for six editions
outcome or per-unit terms appearing in any mid-market ERP quote
weakeners: outcome pricing reverting to consumption floors and minimums — NOW THE NORM (HubSpot seats + credits, S02): read the seat / metered / per-result shares of every hybrid quote separately; treat 'outcome pricing' on a seat floor as consumption pricing with a bonus

patterns.title: Data readiness is the binding constraint
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: verification became a PRODUCT CATEGORY — five launches in nine days (Exaforce kill switch, Cohesity Agent Resilience rollback, Arcjet runtime guard, Alation lineage/compliance, Proofpoint) plus Eve Security funding and Akamai's autonomy-vs-verifiability brief (S06). Cohesity/Vanson Bourne survey (n=3,200, 11 countries): 55% unprepared to detect/contain unintended agent actions; 81% recovery plans need change. Anthropic monitor stats: ~30k concurrent agents, ~0.002% of >1B August decisions blocked (~20k/month). HubSpot: outcomes tracked context quality (S02). Cannabis vertical vendors shipping AI on top of Metrc-shaped compliance data (S14). None of the new controls is priced; the first rollback covers AWS Bedrock only.
confirmers: settled enough to act on; the pilot template's verification gate (M24) now has a market to buy from
weakeners: a wave of audited mid-market ROI results would soften the no-impact half of the consensus — none observed

patterns.title: The plumbing is standardizing: MCP + A2A move from experiment to default
orgs: United Nations / Google Data Commons (public data via connector)
HubSpot (connectors in Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot; three-tier APIs)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: REACH after control — Safari 27 ships a native MCP server (Sep 17; no MDM off-switch yet), UN System Data Commons is MCP-enabled (Sep 18), Emerald Intel ships a cannabis-vertical MCP (Sep 22), HubSpot claims top CRM connector inside Claude/ChatGPT (S02, S12, S13). WEAKENER FIRED for the first time at vendor scale: Salesforce's AIforce/Enterprise AI Harness + Bridget screen-learning integration agent route around approved connectors (S03, S04); Amazon admits agents on its own terms, not a standard's (S01). Acumatica first-party connector: decided by presence/silence at the Oct 1 launch (S07). Caveat: UN Data Commons and Microsoft Agent Framework items rest on a T4 aggregator; primary pages not read.
confirmers: a first-party connector from Acumatica at the Oct 1 R2 launch (NetSuite set the reference posture)
the first first-party connectors from WMS / TMS vendors
weakeners: value migrating to proprietary layers built on top of or around the open core — FIRED E08 at vendor scale (Salesforce harness + Bridget, S03/S04; Amazon's own-terms admission, S01)
any ERP vendor treating screen-driven agents as unauthorised clients (would cut the other way — confirms the open route)

patterns.title: Foundation forecasters are the new baseline — routing and hybrids win
orgs: Academic benchmark wave (2026: volatility, returns, multi-regime)
TIME benchmark authors (NTU / Griffith / Tsinghua / Datadog / Squirrel AI)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: QUIET — no new benchmark, replication or vendor routing control surfaced. E07's TIME benchmark stands as strongest evidence. Quiet-cycle counter = 1; a second quiet edition triggers the deep-dive rule.
confirmers: a planning vendor exposing model choice as a control rather than a hidden default
a second demand-domain replication at an operator (Alibaba E06 remains the only one)
weakeners: a next-generation model decisively closing the gap across EVERY series type, which would make routing unnecessary

patterns.title: AI is a demand-side force: the compute buildout moves freight, power and components
orgs: Kinaxis (data-centre build-outs named as a demand vertical)
C.H. Robinson (first flatbed forecast naming data-centre construction)
patterns.verdict_1line: E08: the pattern acquired a COMMERCIAL FORECAST — C.H. Robinson's first flatbed outlook (Sep 3): 2026 +28%, 2027 +10%, data-centre construction named; dry van 2026 +30% (trimmed), 2027 +10% on SUPPLY contraction. DAT flatbed $2.66/mi +31.2% y/y (wk ending Sep 4); ACT Research up to +41% y/y. WorldACD wk 37: worldwide spot +3% w/w, APAC spot $4.69/kg third consecutive rise, APAC->US tonnage +17%, Korea +53% on semis. TRIPWIRE NOT FIRED: July flatbed -1.6% m/m is the first monthly decline; August figure (CHR October update) is the second-month test; capacity is contracting (opposite of 'stable'). Note the masking risk: next year's rise is forecast on supply contraction, which could hide the buildout's expiry.
confirmers: carrier and trucking results quantifying AI-cargo share
weakeners: two consecutive months of falling ABSOLUTE spot levels with stable capacity — July flatbed -1.6% m/m is month one; August (CHR Oct update) is the test; capacity contracting = condition not met
the share of the announced pipeline actually breaking ground falling materially below ~1/3

Agent-platform pricing: a vendor-published mid-market price list for a SUPPLY CHAIN agent. E08: still none — HubSpot's $0.50/$1 and the E07 CS rates are the only published per-outcome anchors; Agentforce Operations (S04) and Glo 2.0 (S05) both unpriced.

P6 follow-through: quiet in E08 (counter = 1). REMAINING GAPS: (a) a second demand-domain replication at an operator; (b) planning vendors exposing model-routing controls. A second quiet edition triggers the deep-dive rule.

Cannabis lens: ACTIVE in E08 with TWO AI announcements (S13 Emerald Intel MCP, Sep 22; S14 PROTEUS420 PheeBee, Sep 21, plus TSRgrow GROWHub analytics/Metrc and Flourish predictive yield). First edition with AI products rather than a regulatory change; sweep-term review not needed. Standing questions: Metrc-class rail owner shipping first-party AI/MCP (now holds payment behaviour); POS leaders (Dutchie, Flowhub) answering PheeBee; first published dispensary result from an in-stack assistant; the 40-60% AI-influenced-transactions projection (E05 S11) still unmeasured.

Siemens Erlangen 'fully AI-driven factory' (from 2026): watch for published OPERATING results. E08 check: the only published Erlangen numbers are the April 16 Humanoid HMND 01 trial (60 totes/hr, >8h uptime, >90% pick success) — a robot demonstration predating this briefing, not factory operating results. Nothing new.

Salesforce 'Marshall' RESOLVED as to function (E08 S04: Agentforce Operations / ex-Regrello process engine; 30+ blueprints incl. invoice auditing, PO rescheduling; Bridget screen-learning integration agent; vendor claims cycle time -50-70%, manual entry -80%). REMAINING: (a) a published price per process / unit of work; (b) whether the long-horizon runtime spreads beyond the sales agent and the Nov GA date holds; (c) rivals answering with role-agents + per-unit pricing in Q4; (d) any ERP vendor treating Bridget-style screen agents as unauthorised clients.
Kenco's 20-agent commitment — clock from Aug 5. E08: no news. Watch the interim count and any DISCLOSED service-level or cost movement.

Verification tooling as a product category — FIRED E08 (S06: Exaforce, Cohesity, Arcjet, Alation, Proofpoint), UNPRICED. Remaining: (a) first published price for containment/rollback; (b) Cohesity Agent Resilience Microsoft coverage (AWS Bedrock only at launch; GA by end-2026); (c) Microsoft's own answer for Fabric / Power Automate agents (asked via M24); (d) a second independent containment-readiness survey; (e) first insurer/auditor requiring such a control.

NEW E08: Safari 27 native MCP server with no MDM off-switch (per Apple enterprise notes). Watch for Apple adding a device-management control, Chrome/Edge equivalents, and the first enterprise incident attributed to a browser-driven agent.

NEW E08: Amazon's two-door posture (Muse blocked Sep 20; seller plugin for Claude/Quick Sep 23). Watch: Meta-Amazon terms; seller plugin for non-Anthropic assistants; other marketplaces / B2B portals copying identify-and-opt-in rules; whether the plugin uses MCP (unstated).

Product debt: (1) tier T1 labelled 'Analyst / peer-reviewed research' — E08 files Info-Tech (S03) there; add a preprint tier or relabel when harness edits are authorised. (2) assertions.js still hardcodes "search 'stateless' finds S12" — the MCP card must stay S12 and contain 'stateless'. (3) MIMICS effort key: the renderer maps only low/med/watch (watch -> 'Verify'); E07 shipped M13/M9 with eff:'verify' which rendered 'UNDEFINED' — use eff:'watch' for verify-type actions until the renderer is generalised. (4) Nav labels (Verdict/Timeline/Actions) differ from section headings (Obsolescence check / Evolution arc / Transfer to our stack) — role-play friction, cosmetic.

lessons: Role-play persona must state reader tech fluency explicitly; defaults drift to the builder's level (E01 draft-1 failure).
Glossary (TERMS) and Stack-detail line are template-level; append terms, never strip the layer.
Check publisher families before setting multi:true.
Timeline right-hand markers are third-party forecasts, label as such.

Template Rev E (Jul 3): dual REGISTERS — write exec copy (xone/xwhy) separately from analyst copy for every signal; palette bound to view (warm exec / cool analyst, green brand accent); DELTA object + pattern move chips power the weekly pulse strip; append weekly item to feed.xml; update data-ed numeral; PWA assets (icons/manifest/sw) are permanent — never remove.

Rev F editorial rules (Jul 3): never embed UI pills in running prose; badges nowrap; 62ch reading measures; one green data accent; app icon = approved radar-sweep mark (no redesign/recolor without sign-off); 390px mobile checklist incl. notch clearance runs every edition.

Taxonomy v2 + cannabis lens (Jul 3, Rev G): six locked keys (plan/source/make/deliver/sell/infra); value-chain ribbon + infrastructure foundation band replace filter chips; every research week sweeps all 5 stages + infra + cannabis industry; cann:true signals feed the conditional Industry Lens section (auto-hidden when none qualify); stage-focus line must show honest thin/empty states.

E02 (Jul 9, unattended): mimic-board 'from' links must reference current-edition signal codes — board is edition-scoped (M7-M12), while open_actions in state carries all editions; role-play subagent caught exec-register mechanics leakage in shared 'what' blocks (S12/S13) — shared blocks must pass the exec bar too, since both registers render them.

E03 (Jul 16, unattended): role-play subagents caught (a) date-logic errors in forward-looking copy — check every 'next edition confirms X' claim against the actual calendar (a Jul 23 edition cannot confirm a Jul 28 ship); (b) orphan numbers referencing prior editions ($262B) — attribute cross-edition figures explicitly; (c) internal shorthand (Onematica, SADA) needs TERMS glosses since every edition has potential first-time readers; (d) the scatter caption had a hardcoded signal range (S01-S15) — now genericized, keep it generic; (e) assertions.js still hardcodes 'search stateless finds S12' — keep the MCP-spec card at code S12 (or generalize the assertion when next editing the harness is authorized).

E04 (Jul 23, unattended): role-play caught a WEEKDAY error repeated 6x in the marquee signal (called Jul 28 'Monday'; it is Tuesday) — verify the weekday of every dated claim against a calendar before shipping; date arithmetic ('five days out') can be right while the weekday is wrong.

E04: compile-machinery narration ('this compile ran it', 'surfaced by this week's sweep', 'the card is conservatively single-source') in shared 'what' blocks reads as production mechanics to the exec register — keep provenance honesty, but phrase it in reader terms; detailed provenance lives in the Method box.

E04: TAKES must be business-consequence framed in both registers — an IT-status takeaway ('validate servers against the spec') fails the exec CEO-retell test; the freight-cost story beat it for the third slot. Bare M-code chains (M11 → M3) don't belong in exec-visible surfaces.
E04: P7 added — first pattern-set change; procedure held (E03 candidate flag → multi-source corroboration → Method-box note). Two-cycle candidate rule feels right for pattern additions.

E05 (Jul 30, unattended): the two-quiet-cycles rule fired mid-build (P3) and the resulting deep-dive changed the edition (S13 added after first verification pass). Run the quiet-cycle count during step 0, before research ends — deep-dives belong in the research phase, not the fix loop.

E05: role-play caught a stat quoted with its source's own loose arithmetic ('doubling' for 22%→58%). Recompute every ratio in copy even when the source's framing is being quoted; state the numbers instead of the multiplier when in doubt.

E05: exec-register leakage recurred in shared 'what' blocks on the two most technical cards (S12/S10 first drafts read like release notes). For infrastructure signals, draft the shared 'what' in business language FIRST and push every mechanism to the tech line; the exec bar applies to shared blocks (E02 lesson) and infrastructure cards are where it breaks.

E06 (Aug 6, unattended): role-play caught the dated-to-origin convention applied inconsistently — a card mixing a May-origin study with an Aug 1 component carried THIS WEEK while another origin-dated card didn't; when a card mixes origins, state inside the card which component carries the date and align the Method note.
E06: the pulse strip claimed 'P6 + P7 confirmers fire' when P7's event was a promotion, not a confirmer — promotions and confirmer firings are different events; label them precisely in DELTA items.
E06: 'new signals' reads as 'new this week' to an exec — Method now states counts mean new-to-tracker and cards carry origin dates; keep that sentence.
E06: P7 promoted forming->hardening — second pattern-lifecycle change; promotion bar used: >=3 corroborated cycles + spread across >=3 evidence classes + ~2x org count. Reuse this bar.
E06: first cannabis zero week — section auto-hid as designed; zero-state noted in Method and watch list. Two more consecutive zeros should trigger a sweep-term review, not silent acceptance.

E07 (Sep 17, unattended): SIX-WEEK GAP — E06 was W32, E07 is W38, no editions in between. When a gap happens, say so in the masthead meta line and the FIRST Method note, not only in the verdict box; state explicitly that counts and pattern moves reflect the whole window and are not weekly deltas; and restrict THIS WEEK chips to a stated final slice of the window.

E07: pattern STRENGTH is a cumulative count and can only rise, so 'all seven patterns advanced' is arithmetic, not a finding. Never put it in the pulse strip. The direction label is the judgement; say so in the patterns section sub-line.

E07: the pulse strip must fit at 1440px without horizontal scroll — the NEXT EDITION chip has margin-left:auto and silently falls off the right edge when items are long. Budget ~100 visible characters across the three items; verify with el.scrollWidth - el.clientWidth === 0, not by eye.

E07: role-play caught pattern-org DOUBLE-COUNTING (Salesforce appeared twice in P3 under two descriptions, inflating strength by one). Before publishing, normalise every org list by stripping the parenthetical and checking for duplicate stems.

E07: the exec role-play found the highest-impact signal for our own stack (Acumatica R2, impact 5 / adopt 5) absent from the five-minute layer. TAKES must be chosen by consequence-to-us, not by novelty — the item about software we actually run outranks a bigger external story.

E07: exec-register mechanics leakage recurred in shared 'what' blocks on EIGHT of fourteen cards, worst on the infrastructure and vendor-announcement cards. The E05 lesson holds and needs enforcing earlier: draft every shared 'what' in business language FIRST, lead it with the consequence, and push every mechanism to the tech line before the first verification pass, not after the role-play.

E07: role-play caught internal arithmetic contradictions that the harness cannot see — 'six agents in three months' against an Aug 5 announcement and early-September count; 'none reached the upper three levels' against L3 = 1 company on a six-level scale; 'six weeks after' a Jul 28 event dated Sep 1 (five weeks). RECOMPUTE EVERY INTERVAL AND ORDINAL in copy against the underlying dates before shipping.

E07: a prior edition's own note can be wrong. E06 recorded the Kinaxis Q2 call as falling on its compile day (Aug 6); the coverage located in E07 is dated late August. Carry forward prior-edition claims as claims, check them, and say which version the current edition uses.

E07: when a card mixes a shared 'what' with a preprint source, say 'preprint, not peer-reviewed' IN THE CARD. Tier T1 is labelled 'analyst / peer-reviewed' and arXiv is neither — logged as product debt in the watch list.

E07: the cannabis lens returned with a REGULATORY signal rather than an AI one. That is legitimate (it changes the data foundation) but the card must say so in its own text and the Method note must record that the AI sweep itself returned nothing.

E07: name the source organisation in the PROSE, not only in the source list — the exec role-play refused to repeat 'a major retailer' and 'the benchmark provider' claims to a COO. Every number that will be quoted upward needs a named owner in the sentence that carries it.

E08 (Sep 24, unattended): a watch item declared 'not published' in E07 (the Acumatica R2 date) had been public since Aug 26 — when a watch item says 'not found', run one targeted search for the item by name before carrying it; state misses on the card.

E08: role-play caught a pattern verdict citing a claim that was not on the card it pointed to (GitLab metering attributed to S12 after it was cut from S12's prose). Every 'Sxx' reference in a pattern verdict must be grep-checked against that card's text before verification.

E08: takeaway/one-liner overstatement class — 'seven vendors launched products' when two were a funding round and an advisory brief; 'usage doubled' when three different metrics existed. Count the nouns; name the metric and its baseline; never summarise a range with the loosest number.

E08: exec register still needs ORGANISATION NAMES in takeaways, pulse strip, verdict box and pattern verdicts ('a mainstream vendor', 'the largest broker', 'one AI lab' all failed the CEO-retell test again). The E07 lesson holds; apply it to the judgement layer, not only the cards.
